info.description:
# Authentication The Appstorespy API uses API-KEY authentication.
If you do not have an API Key token, you can get it on your account page [https://appstorespy.com/account](https://appstorespy.com/account).
An API Key is required to be sent as part of every request in request header. ``` -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'API-KEY: ' ``` # Agents and MCP AI agents can call the same endpoints as MCP tools at [https://api.appstorespy.com/mcp](https://api.appstorespy.com/mcp), with the same API-KEY header and the same credits per call.
[https://api.appstorespy.com/agentic-access](https://api.appstorespy.com/agentic-access) lists what each operation costs and whether it reads, queues or writes; [https://api.appstorespy.com/skills/](https://api.appstorespy.com/skills/) holds one agent skill per capability; [https://api.appstorespy.com/llms.txt](https://api.appstorespy.com/llms.txt) links every agent document. # Fields Use the fields parameter to specify which fields should be returned.
Example: ``` Request: fields=name,developer_name,ipd,downloads,... Response: {name: ..., developer_name: ..., ipd: ..., downloads: ..., ...} ``` Don`t use fields parameter if you need to get all fields.
# Sort When you use search, you can add a sort parameter. ``` Request: sort=ratingCount Response: [{name: app1, ratingCount: 4.2}, {name: app2, ratingCount: 4.4}, ...] ``` If you need DESC sorting add "-" before sort parametr. ``` Request: sort=-ratingCount Response: [{name: app2, ratingCount: 4.4}, {name: app1, ratingCount: 4.2}, ...] ``` # County & Language params ... # Status codes / Error codes * 200 OK. * 202 Accepted - The app was not present in our databases and has been submitted for crawling. If the app is available anywhere, it will be available soon. * 204 No Content - No data for requested country. * 403 Forbidden - Your access token is not valid. * 429 Too Many Requests - Your request rate is over the limit.

get.summary: Get the Google Play listing of an app in any language.
get.description: Returns the store listing of one app for a country and language exactly as Google Play serves it: title, short and full description, what's new, icon, feature graphic, trailer and screenshots. Any language Google Play Console accepts can be requested. The listing is crawled on demand and kept; `freshness` sets how old a kept listing may be before it is crawled again. A call waits for a running crawl for up to about 30 seconds and answers 202 with the crawl state if it is still running; repeat the same request to get the listing. Pass `wait=false` to get the 202 immediately. Repeated requests for the same listing share one crawl. `translated` tells whether Google Play machine-translated the texts instead of showing a translation the developer supplied. The call that queues a crawl costs the crawl price, even when it answers 202; a call served from a kept listing, including a kept not-found, costs the read price; a 202 to a call that found the crawl already running costs nothing, and so do a 422, a 429 and any 5xx, a failed crawl (502) included.

get.summary: Get Apps Installs Daily
get.description:
Get Google Play apps daily installs.

`ipd` is derived from the cumulative install total: each increase is spread evenly across the elapsed days since the total last changed, so collection gaps and lagging reports are amortised rather than reported as a single-day spike. Values are raw and never negative.

By default these are unsmoothed figures. AppstoreSpy's Daily Installs chart additionally applies a moving average for readability. Pass `smooth=true` to get that series: a centered, triangular-weighted 9-day moving average of `ipd` (weights 1,2,3,4,5,4,3,2,1; days without data are skipped and the weights renormalised). Neighbouring days outside `start`/`end` are included in the window, so the first and last days are smoothed the same way as the rest.

PlayListing.description:
A Google Play store listing crawled live for one country and language.

Unlike `PlayApp`, nothing here comes from AppstoreSpy storage: the fields are
exactly what Google Play served for the requested `country` and `language` at
`crawled`, so any locale Google Play Console accepts can be requested.
